title: UCAV conceptual design and sub-scale, 3D printed wind tunnel testing
author: Joăo Antônio Dantas de Jesus Ferreira
abstract: The utilization of Remotely Piloted Aircraft is on steep ascent. in this context, many specificities of the Design of such aircraft, that present various characteristics that are uncommon to locally piloted aircraft, aren't clearly present on contemporary literature. This work targets the development of the Conceptual Design of an Remotely Piloted Aircraft with offensive capabilities that satisfies specific requirements of Brazilian Air Force. Due to the gaps found on literature, this work also developed Sub-Scale Models for aerodynamic tests on Wind Tunnel. The model construction was developed with Computer Aided Design softwares, which were used for the generation of multiple configurations to be printed on 3D Printers. This work developed integration solutions between the various printed parts that allowed for rapid configuration change. The developed models were, then, used on Wind Tunnel testing to gather data for the conceptual design, as well as to validate the design. The tests shown that the proposed design was valid and were productive as complementation to the contemporary literature.
